sentences.text: Learned advocate for the appellants pointed out the pleadings, evidence, grounds of objections of the appeals and the reasons and findings of the learned Reference Court in the impugned judgment.

Learned advocate for the appellants submitted that though the sale exemplar at Exh.23 is relied upon by the learned Reference Court, it has not awarded the compensation as per the sale consideration mentioned in it.

The Reference Court has adjusted the some amount and reduced some amount and awarded the compensation @ Rs.23,000/- per Hectare for non irrigated lands and Rs.28,000/- per Hectare for irrigated lands, which is not legal and correct.
He pointed out the reasons and findings of the learned Reference court in that regard.
He submitted that the adjustment of the amount for small/big size of the lands of the claimants in the sale exemplar is not as per the provisions of law.
He therefore, submitted to award the compensation as per the sale exemplar, without deducting any amount.
3. Learned A.G.Ps.
for the respondents

have strongly  fa1238.11-  -4- opposed the appeals and submitted that the reasonable amount of compensation has been determined as per the market value and awarded by the learned Land Reference Court.

There is necessity of Babarao Umaji Khambalkar vs State Of Mah And Anr on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73090589/
3 deduction of some amount, as the claimants' lands are more than one Hectare and the land in sale exemplar is only 20 Are land.
Learned A.G.P. submitted that the S.L.A.O. is not made party in these proceedings.

sentences.text: For that purpose, the learned A.G.Ps. pointed out Exh.29 in which it is stated that the Executive Engineer is the acquiring body but the award has been drawn and signed by the S.L.A.O., Marathwada Krushi Vidyapeeth, Parbhani.
He submitted that the acquiring body is not made party in the Reference before the Reference Court.

The learned A.G.Ps. for the State are relying upon the authority of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Lal Chand vs. Union of India and another, (2009) 15 SCC 769, in which it is held that deduction for development must be made and it varies between 20% to 75% of the development price.

sentences.text:
It is lastly prayed to deduct 65% of the amount out of the said sale exemplar at Exh.23.
4.
On perusal of the impugned judgment and the award alongwith the sale exemplar Exh.23, it is crystal clear that 101 Are land is sold for consideration of Rs.48,000/- that means, Rs.475.24 per Are.
The land in the sale exemplar at Exh.23 is only 20 Are land.
It is a small size of land and the claimants lands are double to that  fa1238.11-  -5- land i.e. more than one Hectare.
Therefore, in view of the authority of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Lal Chand vs. Union of India and another (supra), 20% deduction would be the proper deduction.

sentences.text:
The learned Reference Court while determining the value of the acquired land, in para 14,
held that after making necessary deduction and adjustments, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.38,000/- per Hectare for irrigated land.
The sale exemplar is of irrigated land.

Thus,
interference is warranted in the impugned judgment and award at the hands of this Court, as the sale exemplar Exh.23 was not properly appreciated by the learned Reference Court.
5. In so far as the first appeal No. 1169 of 2011 is concerned

,
admittedly, the land of the appellant in the said appeal is non irrigated land and therefore, the appellant in the said appeal is entitled to 50%
of the said amount i.e. Rs.19,000/- per Hectare i.e. Rs.190/- per Are,
Rs.7600/- per Acre.
The appeals therefore, deserve to be partly allowed.

Hence, the following order:-
 fa1238.11-  -6-
ORDER I.
The first appeals are partly allowed.

III. The impugned judgment and awards passed by the learned Reference Court are set aside and they are modified as under:-
a) The appellants in all first appeals, except first appeal No 1169 of 2011, are entitled to compensation @ Rs.38,000/- per Hectare and the appellant in first appeal No.
1169 of 2011 is entitled to to compensation @ Rs.19,000/- per Hectare, including amount of compensation which was awarded and received by the appellants, with all other statutory benefits i.e. additional component, interest and solatium as per the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
IV) The appellants are not entitled to interest amount for the delayed period, which was condoned by this Court.
